mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over two consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a financial crisis when risk premia spike independently.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) contraction signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST monthly decline > 10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 70% of triggered episodes, or the GDP and housing signal fires but market rallies on strong earnings surprises.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in the unemployment rate above 5% for three consecutive months indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which erodes consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of strong productivity growth offsetting labor weakness.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average by more than 3% for four consecutive months signals broad-based supply chain stress, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-mo MA by > 3% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly different from zero during triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a period of falling commodity prices that offset input cost pressures.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both CPIAUCSL (inflation) and FEDFUNDS below 2% indicates a deflationary environment with accommodative policy, which historically supports risk assets by lowering real interest rates and boosting equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 2% AND FEDFUNDS < 2% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a banking crisis where liquidity dries up despite low rates.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) of more than 300,000 coincident with an unemployment rate below 4% signals an overheating labor market, which raises wage inflation and increases recession risk, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when fiscal stimulus offsets labor-market overheating.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) of more than 1% alongside a concurrent drop in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 8% signals a sharp near-term demand shock, which depresses earnings expectations and yields negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly change < -1% AND HOUST monthly change < -8%
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 70% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a geopolitical shock that drives safe-haven flows to equities.

mechanism_narrative: An extended period (six consecutive months) where FEDFUNDS remain above 5.5% with CPIAUCSL below 3% indicates a restrictive monetary stance amid low inflation, which historically has been associated with equity market underperformance due to higher financing costs and muted earnings growth, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 5.5% AND CPIAUCSL < 3% for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when a major fiscal stimulus offsets the impact of high rates.
